这些结果表明了一个清晰的模式：当 GPT-3 被诸如《消除对妇女一切形式歧视公约》或联合国教科文组织的《人工智能建议书》（两者都是在多个国家背景下共同撰写的建议书）等文本提示时，它更有可能保留源材料的内在价值取向。These results suggest a clear pattern: when GPT-3 is prompted with texts such as CEDAW or UNESCO’s AI Recommendation, both co-authored across multiple national contexts, it is more likely to preserve the embedded value orientation of the source material.

第2章：Chapter 2:机器中的幽灵有美国口音The Ghost in the Machine Has an American Accent

84

出现了两种可能的解释。首先，这些文件的共同作者可能以更加分散和多元化的形式编码价值观，反映来自多种文化、法律和政治角度的贡献。这种分布式编码可以通过稀释任何单一文化框架的主导地位来缓冲价值突变。其次，此类文本通常依赖于共识驱动、基于权利的语言，这些语言经过精心设计，以实现文化中立和广泛接受[271, 220]。这种语言可能会起到稳定器的作用，为 GPT-3 重新解释提供更少的修辞立足点。该模型并未将这些价值观视为有争议的政治立场，而是将它们再现为既定的制度事实。总而言之，这表明，价值多元化在全球范围内协商和批准后，可以充当不易漂移的规范锚。Two possible explanations emerge. First, the collaborative authorship of these documents may encode values in a more distributed and pluralistic form, reflecting contributions from multiple cultural, legal, and political perspectives. This distributed encoding could buffer against value mutation by diluting the dominance of any single cultural frame. Second, such texts often rely on consensus-driven, rights-based language deliberately crafted to be culturally neutral and broadly acceptable [271, 220]. This language may act as a stabiliser, providing fewer rhetorical footholds for GPT-3 to reinterpret. Rather than treating these values as contestable political positions, the model appears to reproduce them as settled institutional facts. Taken together, this suggests that value pluralism, when globally negotiated and ratified, can function as a normative anchor less susceptible to drift.

这些可能性共同为未来的研究提出了重要问题。如果跨不同价值体系的共同作者和基于共识的语言的使用有助于稳定生成模型中的价值传递，那么此类策略可能会为训练数据管理、提示设计和未来的评估框架提供信息。重要的是，他们还指出了模型可能不太容易再现主导文化偏见的条件。这表明，当通过多边进程正式编码时，价值多元化可以作为生成人工智能中对价值漂移的一种认知抵抗形式。Together, these possibilities raise important questions for future research. If coauthorship across diverse value systems and the use of consensus-based language can help stabilize value transmission in generative models, then such strategies may inform training data curation, prompt design, and future evaluation frameworks. Importantly, they also point to conditions under which models may be less prone to reproducing dominant cultural biases. This suggests that value pluralism, when formally encoded through multilateral processes, can serve as a form of epistemic resistance to value drift in generative AI.

2.4 讨论：协调的教训2.4 Discussion: Lessons for Alignment

本研究旨在探讨 GPT-3 在处理输入文本时，特别是那些与统计上占主导地位的美国价值观 (RQ1) 不同的文本时，会在多大程度上改变或重新构建文化中嵌入的道德价值观。此外，我们的目的是展示描述性的、多元化的评估方法，在世界价值观调查等经验数据集的基础上，如何能够为生成人工智能模型（RQ2）提供更具包容性和文化敏感性的评估。This study set out to explore the extent to which GPT-3 alters or reframes culturally embedded ethical values when processing input texts, especially those diverging from statistically dominant US values (RQ1). Additionally, we aimed to demonstrate how descriptive, pluralist evaluation methods, informed by empirical datasets like the World Values Survey, can provide more inclusive and culturally sensitive evaluations of generative AI models (RQ2).

在解决 RQ1 时，我们的结果清楚地表明，GPT-3 经常改变嵌入在不同文化文本中的价值观，经常通过明显的美国规范框架重新解释它们。一个特别具有代表性的案例是我们涉及《澳大利亚枪支法》的测试。尽管澳大利亚社会有明确的共识，认为公共安全优先于个人枪支所有权，但 GPT-3 的成果将该法案重新定义为对个人自由和自卫权利的威胁，呼应了植根于美国主流文化叙事的关键价值观。这种改变虽然只发生在六项产出中的一项中，但强调了价值漂移的概率性但具有伦理意义的本质；当模型广泛部署时，即使是不常见的突变也可能产生重大影响。In addressing RQ1, our results clearly show that GPT-3 often altered the values embedded in culturally diverse texts, frequently reinterpreting them through distinctly US normative frames. A particularly illustrative case was our test involving the Australian Firearms Act. Despite clear Australian societal consensus prioritising public safety over individual firearm ownership, GPT-3 produced outputs reframing the Act as a threat to individual liberty and self-defence rights, echoing key values rooted in dominant US cultural narratives. The alteration, although occurring in only one of six outputs, underscores the probabilistic but ethically significant nature of value drift; even infrequent mutations can carry substantial implications when models are deployed widely.

第2章：Chapter 2:机器中的幽灵有美国口音The Ghost in the Machine Has an American Accent

85

在我们对性别角色的分析中，带有美国色彩的重构证据是值得注意的，西蒙娜·德·波伏瓦 (Simone de Beauvoir) 的 GPT-3 的输出就是例证。Evidence of reframing with an American undertone was notable in our analysis of gender roles, as exemplified by GPT-3’s outputs from Simone de Beauvoir's第二性The Second Sex。在这里，GPT-3 倾向于将波伏娃对父权统治的批判性女权主义审视转变为人们熟悉的美国浪漫欲望和性别本质主义理想的比喻。这些产出将结构性批评扁平化为个性化叙事（反映美国主导文化态度），并严重扭曲了原文的预期含义和伦理视角。. Here, GPT-3 tended to convert de Beauvoir’s critical feminist examination of patriarchal dominance into familiar American tropes of romantic desire and gender-essentialist ideals. These outputs flattened structural critiques into individualised narratives (reflecting dominant US cultural attitudes) and significantly distorted the intended meaning and ethical perspective of the original text.

同样，我们对 GPT-3 对安吉拉·默克尔关于难民接收的演讲的处理方式的分析表明，默克尔对难民支持的人道主义和宪法承诺明显转变为优先考虑移民控制、有条件援助和国家安全的叙述。产出通常采用美国移民话语中典型的资源敏感、安全化言论，强调自由裁量的国家利益高于道德义务。这与特朗普政府期间盛行的主流言论明显一致，进一步表明训练数据中的历史背景如何隐式指导生成模型输出。Similarly, our analysis of GPT-3's handling of Angela Merkel's speech on refugee intake illuminated a clear shift from Merkel’s humanitarian and constitutional commitment to refugee support towards narratives prioritising immigration control, conditional aid, and national security. Outputs commonly employed a resource-sensitive, securitised rhetoric typical of US immigration discourse, emphasising discretionary national interest over moral obligation. This was notably aligned with the dominant rhetoric prevalent during the Trump administration, further indicating how historical context in training data can implicitly guide generative model outputs.

谈到 RQ2，我们的研究强调了基于经验、跨文化数据（例如世界价值观调查）的描述性多元方法的方法论价值。传统的规范基准常常掩盖自己的文化假设，提出受环境限制的标准，就好像它们是通用的一样。例如，毒性测试嵌入了英美文明规范，导致非西方言论的错误分类[347]同样，常识和推理基准（例如维诺格拉德图式或社会智商）反映了西方文化规范，但呈现出它们的答案，就好像它们表达了普遍共享的真理一样[99]。相比之下，描述性多元方法使这些假设变得可见，从而能够对生成输出进行更透明的评估。Turning to RQ2, our study highlights the methodological value of a descriptive pluralist approach grounded in empirical, cross-cultural data such as the World Values Survey. Traditional normative benchmarks often obscure their own cultural assumptions, presenting context-bound standards as if they were universal. For instance, toxicity tests embed Anglo-American norms of civility, leading to the misclassification of non-Western speech [347] Similarly, commonsense and reasoning benchmarks such as the Winograd Schema or Social IQ reflect Western cultural norms, yet present their answer keys as if they expressed universally shared truths [99]. By contrast, a descriptive pluralist method makes these assumptions visible, enabling a more transparent evaluation of generative outputs.

通过将 GPT-3 的输出与有关国家价值观的可靠实证数据（例如，美国与澳大利亚对枪支管制的态度）配对，我们展示了描述性的跨文化方法如何能够更清晰地识别规范偏见。这个视角支持文化上细致入微的评估，而不是假设普遍性。如果没有这种多元化的基础，评估者就有可能强化他们打算批评的主导或霸权文化框架[43]。By pairing GPT-3 outputs with robust empirical data on national values (e.g., US versus Australian attitudes to gun control), we show how descriptive, cross-cultural approaches enable clearer identification of normative biases. This lens supports culturally nuanced assessment rather than presuming universality. Without such pluralist grounding, evaluators risk reinforcing the very dominant or hegemonic cultural frames they intend to critique [43].

此外，我们从涉及国际共同撰写的文件（例如来自联合国和教科文组织的文件）的测试中得出的结果为减轻价值漂移提供了有希望的策略。事实证明，体现分布式价值编码和共识驱动语言的文本更能抵抗突变，这表明全球协商框架可以充当稳定锚。虽然这并不能解决现场环境中持续微调的问题，但它确实指出了一个实用的方向：将这种多元化、基于共识的文本纳入培训和评估管道中，作为参考点或压力测试。做事Additionally, our findings from tests involving internationally co-authored documents (such as those from the UN and UNESCO) offer promising strategies for mitigating value drift. Texts embodying distributed value encoding and consensus-driven language proved more resistant to mutation, suggesting that globally negotiated frameworks may act as stabilising anchors. While this does not solve the problem of continual fine-tuning in live environments, it does point to a practical direction: incorporating such pluralist, consensusbased texts into training and evaluation pipelines as reference points or stress tests. Doing

86

因此不会消除价值漂移，但它可以为开发人员和政策制定者提供更清晰的基线来检测、预测和管理价值漂移。so will not eliminate value drift, but it could provide developers and policymakers with clearer baselines for detecting, anticipating, and managing it.

我们的研究结果强调了一个更广泛的道德观点：全球部署的人工智能不应该遵循任何单一的道德准则。使一种框架（无论是自由个人主义、功利主义还是人权话语）普遍化的努力可能会输出一种狭隘的伦理，就好像它是普遍的一样。实际上，这重新体现了现有的权力不对称并使替代传统边缘化。多元取向将普遍准则的缺失重新定义为一种设计条件，而不是一个问题：评估应该揭示模型如何驾驭有争议的价值观，而不是衡量对预定层次结构的符合程度。Our findings underscore a broader ethical point: there is no single moral canon that a globally deployed AI should align with. Efforts to universalise one framework (whether liberal individualism, utilitarianism, or human-rights discourse) risk exporting a parochial ethic as if it were universal. In practice, this re-inscribes existing power asymmetries and marginalises alternative traditions. A pluralist orientation reframes the absence of a universal canon not as a problem but as a design condition: evaluation should reveal how models navigate contested values, rather than measure conformity to a predetermined hierarchy.

最后，虽然我们的研究分析了 2021 年的早期模型迭代，但我们观察到的价值突变在 2025 年仍然高度相关。在相对原始、未经过滤的状态下评估 GPT-3 提供了有价值的历史参考点。这些点是评估一致性方法、RLHF 和宪法人工智能后续进展的重要基准。通过明确记录这些早期的文化偏见，当代的评估者和开发者可以批判性地衡量新方法是否真正减轻了偏见，或者只是将它们掩盖在表面的对齐技术之下。正如达尔格伦等人。 [94] 请注意，诸如 RLHF 之类的一致性方法有可能将道德范围缩小到助人为乐、无害和诚实的简单化代表，同时保持潜在的政治和文化不对称完好无损。我们的研究结果支持了这一担忧：即使没有恶意，GPT3 也会经常通过美国占主导地位的道德语法来重新构建文本，这表明对齐机制必须应对更深层次的结构性偏见，而不是依赖于表面行为修复。Finally, while our study analysed an early model iteration from 2021, the value mutations we observed remain highly relevant in 2025. Evaluating GPT-3 in its relatively raw, unfiltered state provides valuable historical reference points. Such points are essential benchmarks for assessing subsequent advancements in alignment methodologies, RLHF and constitutional AI. By documenting these early cultural biases explicitly, contemporary evaluators and developers can critically gauge whether new methods genuinely mitigate biases or merely obscure them beneath superficial alignment techniques. As Dahlgren et al. [94] caution, alignment approaches such as RLHF risk narrowing ethics to simplistic proxies of helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, while leaving underlying political and cultural asymmetries intact. Our findings support this concern: even without malicious intent, GPT3 routinely reframed texts through a dominant US moral grammar, suggesting that alignment mechanisms must contend with deeper structural biases rather than rely on surface-level behavioural fixes.

这项研究使用定性、描述性方法，特别适合探索像 GPT-3 这样的概率性、认知性开放系统的行为。我们的方法不是预设正确性或一致性的固定基准，而是使我们能够追踪嵌入的价值观是如何在上下文丰富且解释性复杂的文本中重新语境化、重构或保存的。这种仔细阅读在生成时代尤其重要，在这个时代，输出不仅取决于正式的培训目标，还取决于潜在的文化假设、互动历史和模型可供性。This study's use of a qualitative, descriptive approach was particularly well-suited to exploring the behaviour of a probabilistic, epistemically open system like GPT-3. Rather than presupposing fixed benchmarks for correctness or alignment, our methodology enabled us to trace how embedded values were recontextualised, reframed, or preserved in contextually rich and interpretively complex texts. This kind of close reading is especially important in the generative era, where outputs are shaped not only by formal training objectives but also by latent cultural assumptions, interaction history, and model affordances.

总之，这些发现为我们的两个研究问题提供了明确的答案：Together, the findings offer a clear response to our two research questions:

  • RQ1：在处理输入文本时，GPT-3 在多大程度上改变了文化中嵌入的道德价值观，特别是那些与报道的美国主导价值观不同的文本？RQ1: To what extent does GPT-3 alter culturally embedded ethical values when processing input texts, particularly those that diverge from reported dominant US values?

87

研究表明，GPT-3经常通过以美国为中心的价值模式和道德逻辑重新语境化或巧妙地重构这些价值观，往往扭曲了最初的规范意图。The study demonstrates that GPT-3 frequently recontextualised or subtly reframed such values through US-centric value patterns and moral logics, often distorting the original normative intent.

• RQ2：描述性、多元化的评估方法（基于世界价值观调查等经验数据集）如何为生成人工智能模型的更具包容性和代表性的评估的发展提供信息？RQ2: How could a descriptive, pluralist evaluation approach (grounded in empirical datasets like the World Values Survey) inform the development of more inclusive and representative evaluations of generative AI models?

我们的方法表明，描述性多元评估为检测模型偏差和识别更公平、更具包容性的价值调整策略的机会提供了更符合文化的视角。Our method shows that descriptive pluralist evaluations offer a more culturally attuned lens for detecting model bias and identifying opportunities for more equitable and inclusive value alignment strategies.

结果表明，多元化、以经验为基础的评估框架对于持续开发能够在不同社会文化背景下负责任地运行的人工智能系统至关重要。The results suggest that pluralist, empirically grounded evaluation frameworks will be essential in the ongoing development of AI systems capable of operating responsibly across diverse sociocultural contexts.

2.5 结论：走向多元化评价2.5 Conclusion: Toward Pluralist Evaluation

我们的探索性研究提供了早期证据，表明像 GPT-3 这样的生成式人工智能系统可以微妙但显着地改变文化嵌入的价值观，通常通过美国主导的规范镜头重新构建它们。这些发现强调需要继续对生成性产出中的文化偏见进行批判性评估，并支持采用描述性、多元化评估方法的理由。Our exploratory study provides early evidence that generative AI systems like GPT-3 can subtly but significantly mutate culturally embedded values, often reframing them through dominant US normative lenses. These findings underscore the need for continued critical evaluation of cultural biases in generative outputs and support the case for adopting descriptive, pluralist evaluation methods.

我们建议进一步研究两个有希望的领域：首先，扩大基于经验的跨文化数据集（例如世界价值观调查）的使用，以更好地检测和分析价值扭曲；其次，研究这些方法如何为基于分布式价值编码和共识驱动语言的对齐策略提供信息，目的是创建更稳定、更符合道德的人工智能系统。We suggest two promising areas for further research: first, expanding the use of empirically grounded, cross-cultural datasets (such as the World Values Survey) to better detect and analyse value distortions; second, investigating how these methods might inform alignment strategies built on distributed value encoding and consensus-driven language, with the aim of creating more stable and ethically responsive AI systems.

生成式人工智能永远不会摆脱价值观；问题是谁的值在其输出中被放大、静音或覆盖。我们对早期 GPT-3 的研究表明，一个主要接受美国和英语数据训练的系统如何通过美国道德视角重新构建全球文本，这对文化权威如何在人工智能介导的话语中分配产生影响。与此同时，我们发现多元化、共识驱动的文本（例如联合国公约）更能抵抗漂移，这表明了建立更稳健的评估基线的途径。这个教训很明确：负责任的人工智能评估不能集中于单一的道德准则，而必须拥抱多元化、情境敏感性和描述性分析。简而言之，多元评估不是一个可选的附加项，而是在价值多元化的世界中负责任地部署生成式人工智能的最低条件。Generative AI will never be free of values; the question is whose values are amplified, muted, or overwritten in its outputs. Our study of early GPT-3 shows how a system trained on predominantly US and Anglophone data often reframed global texts through an American moral lens, with implications for how cultural authority is distributed in AImediated discourse. At the same time, we found that pluralist, consensus-driven texts, such as UN conventions, were more resistant to drift, suggesting pathways for building more robust evaluative baselines. The lesson is clear: responsible AI evaluation cannot converge on a single ethical canon, but must embrace pluralism, contextual sensitivity, and descriptive analysis. In short, pluralist evaluation is not an optional add-on but the minimum condition for deploying generative AI responsibly in a value-diverse world.

第三章：模型不是市场Chapter 3: The Model is Not the Market

将负责任的人工智能概念应用于房地产行业Applying Responsible-AI concepts to the Real Estate Industry

摘要Abstract

人工智能正在重塑房地产行业，改变估值、物业管理、租户筛选和市场分析。采用速度很快，但监管和教育能力却滞后，导致教育工作者必须应对负责任的人工智能框架、安全辩论和风险管理指导的碎片化局面。本章通过将 Responsible AI 概念转化为应用的房地产环境来解决这一差距。Artificial intelligence is reshaping the real estate industry, transforming valuations, property management, tenant screening, and market analysis. Adoption has been rapid, but regulatory and educational capacity has lagged, leaving educators to navigate a fragmented landscape of Responsible AI frameworks, safety debates, and risk-management guidance. This chapter addresses that gap by translating Responsible AI concepts into an applied real estate context.

本章重点介绍三个基础。首先，模型设计：偏差不仅通过数据产生，还通过架构、优化和目标函数的选择产生。其次，社会技术系统映射：住房市场结果是通过人类参与者、机器系统和制度规则之间的递归交互共同产生的，使责任所在变得可见。第三，市场设计：人工智能系统的结构可以推动或重塑行为，放大或减轻贷款、定价和租户选择等领域的不平等。The chapter focuses on three foundations. First, model design: bias enters not only through data but also through choices of architecture, optimisation, and objective functions. Second, sociotechnical systems mapping: housing-market outcomes are co-produced through recursive interactions among human actors, machine systems, and institutional rules, making visible where accountability lies. Third, market design: AI systems can be structured to nudge or reshape behaviour, amplifying or mitigating inequalities in areas such as lending, pricing, and tenant selection.

通过房地产特定和跨部门的案例研究，本章展示了负责任的人工智能概念如何在实践中运作。这些例子既揭示了希望，也揭示了危险：估值效率的提高，但结构性偏差的强化；改进了租户筛选，但隐私和公平问题也随之增加。Through real estate-specific and cross-sector case studies, the chapter shows how Responsible AI concepts operate in practice. These examples reveal both promise and peril: efficiency gains in valuations, but also the reinforcement of structural bias; improved tenant screening, but with heightened privacy and fairness concerns.

在更广泛的论文中，本章作为一个应用领域案例展示了如何将社会技术评估概念转化为实践，同时保留其教学起源的更独立的风格。它提供了鼓励批判性参与和情境应用的课堂活动和个人作业，展示了负责任的人工智能如何在几乎涉及每个人的领域从原则转向实践。Within the broader thesis, the chapter functions as an applied domain case showing how sociotechnical evaluation concepts can be translated into practice, even while retaining the more standalone style of its pedagogical origins. It offers classroom activities and an individual assignment that encourage critical engagement and contextual application, demonstrating how Responsible AI can move from principle to practice in a domain that touches almost everyone.

3.1 负责任的AI-房地产3.1 Responsible AI-Real Estate

人工智能驱动的技术，包括生成式人工智能，正在改变房地产市场的运作方式以及评估其风险的方式。人工智能 (AI)，包括机器学习 (ML)、深度学习 (DL) 和生成人工智能 (GenAI) 等子领域，正在迅速重塑房地产行业。这些技术已经应用于一系列任务：获得竞争优势、自动化耗时的流程，或者只是跟上行业趋势。表 14 提供了当前房地产中人工智能部署领域的非详尽概述。虽然这些进步提供了明显的效率，但它们也提出了重要的道德、法律和社会问题。这些问题不仅仅来自人工智能系统，而是来自机器输出、制度规则和人类决策共同塑造房地产市场的递归交互。考虑到这些挑战，对负责任人工智能 (RAI) 的透彻理解现在应该成为任何大学房地产课程的一部分。AI-driven technologies, including generative AI, are transforming how real estate markets operate and how their risks must be evaluated. Artificial Intelligence (AI), including subfields like Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Generative AI (GenAI), is rapidly reshaping the real estate industry. These technologies are already being applied across a range of tasks: gaining a competitive edge, automating time-consuming processes, or simply keeping up with industry trends. Table 14 provides a non-exhaustive overview of the areas where AI is currently being deployed in real estate. While these advances offer clear efficiencies, they also raise important ethical, legal, and societal questions. These questions do not arise from AI systems alone, but from the recursive interactions through which machine outputs, institutional rules, and human decisions jointly shape real estate markets. Given these challenges, a thorough understanding of Responsible AI (RAI) should now be integral to any university real estate curriculum.

表 14：人工智能在房地产中应用的任务类型。Table 14: Types of Tasks that AI is Applied to in Real Estate.

财产估价。市场分析和预测分析，例如定价趋势。物业管理包括租户申请和价格设定。投资建议。潜在客户一代。智能建筑，包括能源效率和安全系统。Property valuations. Market analysis and predictive analytics such as pricing trends. Property management including tenant applications and price setting. Investment advice. Lead generation. Smart buildings including energy efficiency and security systems.

房地产营销；包括编写列表和增强照片。Real estate marketing; including writing listings and enhancing photos.

RAI 是一个快速发展的领域，致力于解决部署人工智能系统所涉及的道德、法律和社会风险。与医疗保健、金融或刑事司法（受到广泛审查）等领域不同，房地产在涉及人工智能的更深层次影响方面相对缓慢。该领域的大多数文献都侧重于实际和技术优势，例如提高自动化或效率，而对负责任部署所需的道德框架的关注相对较少。RAI is a rapidly growing field that addresses the ethical, legal, and social risks involved in deploying AI systems. Unlike fields such as healthcare, finance, or criminal justice (which have received broad scrutiny) real estate has been comparatively slow to engage with the deeper implications of AI. Most literature in this space focuses on practical and technical benefits, such as increased automation or efficiency, with relatively little attention given to the ethical frameworks required for responsible deployment.

最近的房地产人工智能研究正确地指出了数据质量、算法透明度以及风险与合规性等问题。然而，这些担忧并没有涵盖人工智能与住房、投资和城市发展交叉时出现的全部道德和安全挑战。因此，教育工作者和实践者Recent research in real estate AI has rightly flagged issues such as data quality, algorithmic transparency, and risk and compliance. However, these concerns do not capture the full range of ethical and safety challenges that arise when AI intersects with housing, investment, and urban development. As a result, educators and practitioners in

房地产行业往往只能进行零散的研究，而负责任的实施指导却有限。real estate are often left navigating fragmented research with limited guidance for responsible implementation.

在更广泛的负责任的人工智能文献中开发的许多见解和框架都可以转移到这个领域。在本论文中，房地产作为一个应用案例，展示了社会技术评估概念如何付诸实践，特别是在生成式人工智能系统调解访问、建议、定价和市场认知的情况下。通过 MaSH Loops 的视角，这些结果不仅是由模型决定的，而且是由技术系统、制度设置和人类吸收之间的递归相互作用决定的。Many of the insights and frameworks developed in broader Responsible AI literature are transferable to this domain. In this thesis, real estate functions as an applied case for showing how sociotechnical evaluation concepts travel into practice, especially where generative AI systems mediate access, advice, pricing, and market perception. Through a MaSH Loops lens, these outcomes are shaped not by models alone, but by recursive interactions among technical systems, institutional settings, and human uptake.

These are critical first steps for students but require expansion.

Misaligned or biased models can reinforce structural inequalities and lead to unintended consequences.

这些源自人工智能伦理和安全的概念工具可以帮助房地产教育工作者和学生分析如何在上下文中评估生成式人工智能系统，包括机器输出、机构设置和人类决策如何在塑造市场结果方面相互作用。随着该领域的成熟，全面的 RAI 方法将支持更公平的市场、减少伤害并提高整个房地产生态系统的信任和透明度。These conceptual tools, drawn from AI ethics and safety, can empower real estate educators and students alike to analyse how generative AI systems should be evaluated in context, including how machine outputs, institutional settings, and human decisions interact in shaping market outcomes. As the field matures, a well-rounded approach to RAI will support fairer markets, reduce harm, and improve trust and transparency across the real estate ecosystem.

3.2 RAI与房地产的现有研究3.2 Existing research in RAI and real estate

RAI 的核心原则（包括数据质量、透明度、问责制、风险管理、合规性和以人为本的设计）在处理大量个人和财务数据的房地产领域尤为重要。这些基础主题为教育工作者在 AIReal Estate 课程中介绍 RAI 概念提供了重要的框架。Core principles of RAI (including data quality, transparency, accountability, risk management, compliance, and human-centered design) hold particular importance in real estate, where vast volumes of personal and financial data are processed. These foundational topics provide a vital framework for educators introducing RAI concepts in AIReal Estate courses.

3.2.1 数据3.2.1 Data

低质量的数据会导致有缺陷的结果这一原则早已被人们所认识。 IBM 的 George Fuechsel 在 20 世纪 50 年代创造了术语 Garbage-In-Garbage-Out (GIGO) [331]。当今数据集规模庞大且通常是非结构化的，GIGO 的影响只会愈演愈烈。数学家 Clive Humby 曾将数据称为“新石油”[235]，而借助现代神经网络，模型可以揭示大量且通常是混乱的数据源中的模式[232]。在房地产领域，不完整的人口统计信息或过时的财产记录可能会影响自动估值模型 (AVM)，从而影响定价和投资决策。The principle that poor-quality data leads to flawed outcomes has long been acknowledged. George Fuechsel of IBM coined the term Garbage-In-Garbage-Out (GIGO) in the 1950s [331]. With today’s large and often unstructured datasets, the impact of GIGO has only intensified. Mathematician Clive Humby famously called data "the new oil" [235], and with modern neural networks, models can uncover patterns in vast, often messy, data sources [232]. In real estate, incomplete demographic information or outdated property records can skew automated valuation models (AVMs), affecting pricing and investment decisions.

现在，道德问题已不仅仅局限于数据质量，还涉及其来源和使用。需要考虑的问题：数据是否尊重隐私权？它是否适合该任务或只是易于访问[208]以及谁拥有它？在众包的情况下，谁是“人群”？他们是合适的人选吗[102]？在使用像亚马逊的 Mechanical Turk [309] 这样的人群驱动平台时，我们必须考虑哪些道德因素，例如工人薪酬及其主观偏见和立场。例如，如果众包的房产图像标签受到工作人员的主观判断的影响，则可能会产生有偏见的 AVM，并无意中伤害某些买家、卖家或租户。Ethical concerns now extend beyond data quality to its provenance and usage. Questions to consider: Does the data respect privacy rights? Is it appropriate for the task or simply easy to access [208] and who owns it? In the case of crowd-sourcing, who is “the crowd” and are they the right people to be sourcing [102]? What ethical considerations must we consider when using crowd-driven platforms like Amazon’s Mechanical Turk [309] such as worker compensation and their subjective biases and standpoints. For example, if crowdsourced labelling of property images is skewed by workers’ subjective judgements, it may produce biased AVMs and inadvertently harm certain buyers, sellers, or tenants.

3.2.2 透明度和可解释性3.2.2 Transparency and Explainability

人工智能的透明度是指让所有利益相关者（从行业专业人士到监管机构和消费者）都能理解自动化决策过程。由于专有限制或纯粹的复杂性，许多房地产算法都是“黑匣子”。黑盒算法是指一种计算过程，其内部逻辑或参数交互要么未公开，要么过于复杂，以至于人类无法轻易解释特定输入如何产生特定输出，即使模型的内部工作原理并未真正隐藏[120, 215]。缺乏可解释性会破坏信任并导致歧视模式持续存在。Transparency in AI is about making automated decision-making processes understandable to all stakeholders, from industry professionals to regulators and consumers. Many real estate algorithms are "black boxes," either due to proprietary restrictions or sheer complexity. A black box algorithm refers to a computational process whose internal logic or parameter interactions are either undisclosed or so complex that humans cannot readily interpret how specific inputs produce certain outputs, even if the model’s inner workings are not literally hidden [120, 215]. This lack of explainability undermines trust and allows discriminatory patterns to persist.

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场The Model is Not the Market

96

在房地产领域，黑盒算法可能会降低租金设定或房产估价等任务的透明度，常常让租户、买家甚至房地产专业人士不清楚如何达到特定结果。In real estate, black-box algorithms can reduce transparency in tasks such as rentsetting or property valuation, often leaving tenants, buyers, and even real estate professionals unclear on how particular outcomes are reached.

例如，不透明的租金设定工具可能会根据有偏见的历史数据抬高某些社区的价格。相比之下，透明的系统使用户能够追踪决策的制定方式，从而鼓励问责制和公平性。可解释人工智能 (XAI) 的进步正在帮助应对这一挑战 [3, 26]。For instance, an opaque rent-setting tool might inflate prices in certain neighbourhoods based on biased historical data. Transparent systems, by contrast, enable users to trace how decisions are made, encouraging accountability and equity. Advances in Explainable AI (XAI) are helping address this challenge [3, 26].

3.2.3 问责制3.2.3 Accountability

问责制问：当人工智能系统造成伤害时，谁该负责？在房地产领域，由于利益相关者链很长，答案很复杂。美国司法部 (DOJ) 就所谓的算法租赁定价协调起诉 RealPage，随后涉及 Greystar、RealPage 和 LivCor 的拟议和解和最终判决试图限制收入管理软件中竞争性敏感数据的使用和共享 [288]。Accountability asks: Who is responsible when an AI system causes harm? In real estate, the answer is complicated due to the long chain of stakeholders. The US Department of Justice (DOJ) sued RealPage over alleged algorithmic rental-pricing coordination, and subsequent proposed settlements and Final Judgments involving Greystar, RealPage, and LivCor sought to restrict the use and sharing of competitively sensitive data in revenue-management software [288].

正如美国副司法部长丽莎·莫纳科所说，“训练机器违法仍然是违法”。 [289]。这个案例展示了技术、法律和道德责任如何在人工智能驱动的房地产工具中相互交叉。当法院和监管机构仔细审查此类合作时，利益相关者必须制定明确的指导方针，定义人工智能生命周期每个阶段的责任人。As US Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco stated, "Training a machine to break the law is still breaking the law." [289]. This case shows how technical, legal, and moral responsibility intersect in AI-powered real estate tools. As courts and regulators closely examine such collaborations, stakeholders must establish clear guidelines that define who is responsible at each stage of the AI lifecycle.

3.2.4 风险与合规3.2.4 Risk and Compliance

英国公司仲量联行 (JLL) 将房地产中的人工智能风险分为三个主要类别 [416]。UK firm Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL), breaks down AI risk in real estate to three primary categories [416].

  • 数据和隐私风险：Data and Privacy Risks:数据泄露、侵犯隐私、违反数据政策。Data breaches, privacy violation, data policy violation.

  • 监管与合规：Regulatory and Compliance:知识产权 (IP) 和合规问题。intellectual property (IP) and compliance issues.

  • 业务和运营风险：Business and Operational Risks:业务决策误判、工作质量下降、成本超支或投资回报率 (ROI) 低。misjudgement in business decision-making, reduced quality of work, cost overrun or low return on investment (ROI).

由此我们可以看到，房地产人工智能的风险管理不仅限于技术故障，还包括声誉（例如歧视性贷款做法）、运营（例如不正确的估值）和监管（例如不遵守新的人工智能法律）。有效的人工智能治理需要定期审计和系统性偏见检查，而不仅仅是 IT 监督。From this we can see that risk management in real estate AI extends beyond technical glitches to encompass reputational (e.g., discriminatory lending practices), operational (e.g., incorrect valuations), and regulatory (e.g., non-compliance with new AI laws). Effective AI governance requires regular audits and systemic bias checks, extending beyond IT oversight.

世界各国政府都在竞相监管人工智能。澳大利亚数字化转型机构 [106]、欧盟人工智能法案 [122] 和英国议会以人工智能为重点的法案 [399] 等举措涵盖了广泛的范围和执行机制，将合规性转化为Governments worldwide are racing to regulate AI. Initiatives like Australia’s Digital Transformation Agency [106], the EU AI Act [122], and the UK Parliament’s AI-focussed bills [399] span a broad range of scopes and enforcement mechanisms, turning compliance into

97

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场。The Model is Not the Market.

一个不断变化的目标，尤其是跨越国际边界或在不可预测的政治领导下。 RAI 的肤浅“勾选”方法越来越多地被批评为道德空洞，有时被称为“道德清洗”[40, 239]。仅仅提供免责声明或样板行为准则对于解决人工智能管道中的潜在偏见和问题几乎没有帮助[273]。学生不仅必须学习法律，还必须学习适应性强的 RAI 技能，以应对不断变化的法律和道德领域。a moving target, especially across international boundaries or under unpredictable political leaderships. Superficial “box-ticking” approaches to RAI have increasingly been criticized as ethically hollow, sometimes referred to as “ethics washing” [40, 239]. Merely offering disclaimers or boilerplate codes of conduct does little to address underlying biases and problems in the AI pipelines [273]. Students must learn not just the laws, but adaptable RAI skills to navigate shifting legal and ethical terrain.

3.2.5 可信度3.2.5 Trustworthiness

人工智能驱动的房地产工具的可信度取决于一致的可靠性、透明度和公平性；增强买家、卖家和行业专业人士信心的品质。欧盟可信人工智能框架[123]定义了三个支柱：Trustworthiness in AI-driven real estate tools depends on consistent reliability, transparency, and fairness; qualities that foster confidence among buyers, sellers, and industry professionals. The EU framework for trustworthy AI [123] defines three pillars:

  • 是否合法且符合适用法律？Is it lawful and compliant with applicable laws?

  • 这符合道德吗？它是否符合使用人工智能和受人工智能影响的人们的道德和价值观？Is it ethical? Does it align with the ethics and values of the people using and impacted by the AI?

  • 从技术和社会角度来看它是否稳健？Is it robust both from a technical and social perspective?

许多政府和大型科技公司将信任视为人工智能的核心原则。 2023年，拜登政府发布了一项促进“安全可信的人工智能”的行政命令[388]，后来被特朗普总统撤销[359]。对人工智能平台和决策的信任直接影响这些技术的传播和采用[6]。牛津大学 2022 年的一项研究指出，房地产行业不愿采用这些工具，理由是对准确性和公平性的担忧 [424] 因此，任何人工智能在房地产行业的部署都应考虑到这一因素，并正面解决缓解问题。Many governments and major tech firms cite trust as a core AI principle. In 2023, the Biden administration issued an executive order promoting "safe and trustworthy AI" [388], later revoked by President Trump [359]. Trust in AI platforms and decision-making directly impacts diffusion and adoption of these technologies [6]. A 2022 Oxford study noted property industry reluctance to adopt these tools, citing concerns about accuracy and fairness [424] As such any deployment of AI into the real estate sector should take this factor into consideration and address mitigation issues head-on.

3.2.6 以人为本3.2.6 Human-centred

以人为中心的人工智能专注于设计和部署能够增强而不是削弱人类能力和福祉的系统。在房地产领域，平衡效率与用户体验（UX）、公平性和信任的工具可以减轻人们在算法制定关键生活决策（例如租户筛选或财产评估）时面临的漏洞。以人为本的方法考虑更广泛的人类系统（房主、投资者、物业经理和社区成员），确保人工智能增强人类判断力，而不会造成或加剧社会不平等。Human-centered AI focuses on designing and deploying systems that enhance, rather than undermine, human capabilities and well-being. In real estate, tools that balance efficiency with user experience (UX), fairness, and trust can mitigate the vulnerabilities people face when algorithms shape critical life decisions, such as tenant screenings or property appraisals. A human-centered approach considers the broader human system (homeowners, investors, property managers, and community members) ensuring that AI augments human judgment without creating or exacerbating social inequities.

本节介绍了适用于房地产的 RAI 基本原则（数据、透明度、问责制、合规性、可信度和以人为本）。这些概念应构成任何人工智能房地产课程的基础。虽然并不详尽，但它们提供了坚实的道德和实践基础。下一节构建This section has introduced foundational RAI principles (data, transparency, accountability, compliance, trustworthiness, and human-centeredness) as they apply to real estate. These concepts should form the basis of any AI-Real Estate curriculum. While not exhaustive, they offer a robust ethical and practical grounding. The next section builds

98

在此基础上，引入较少探讨但必不可少的 RAI 主题，帮助未来的专业人士预测系统性风险并促进房地产市场的公平。on this foundation, introducing less explored but essential RAI topics that help future professionals anticipate systemic risks and promote equity in the property market.

3.3 超越 RAI 基础知识3.3 Beyond RAI basics

在上述 RAI 基础主题的基础上，本节深入探讨了更高级的概念：模型设计、社会技术映射和市场设计。从自动估值到风险评分，精心设计的模型可以推动更好的房地产决策，而设计不当的模型则可能会放大偏见和误解。Building on the above foundational RAI topics, this section delves into more advanced concepts: model design, sociotechnical mapping, and market design. From automated valuations to risk scoring, well-crafted models can drive better property decisions, while poorly designed models risk amplifying biases and misunderstandings.

虽然基础知识仍然至关重要，但房地产从业者和教育工作者日益面临复杂的挑战，例如协调多个利益相关者的利益、管理广泛的金融风险以及在快速变化的市场条件下保持公平。通过研究人工智能驱动模型的构建方式（3.1 模型设计）、技术和人类元素如何在房地产生态系统中相互作用（3.2 社会技术映射）以及如何系统地塑造模型设计以获得更公平的结果（3.3 市场设计），教育工作者可以更好地让学生做好准备，以应对快速变化的环境。While the basics remain vital, real estate practitioners and educators increasingly confront complex challenges, such as reconciling multiple stakeholders’ interests, managing wide-ranging financial risks, and maintaining fairness in rapidly shifting market conditions. By examining how AI-driven models are constructed (3.1 Model Design), how technological and human elements interact within real estate ecosystems (3.2 Sociotechnical Mapping), and how model designs can be systematically shaped for more equitable outcomes (3.3 Market Design), educators can better prepare students to navigate a rapidly shifting landscape.

3.3.1 模型设计3.3.1 Model Design

模型是现实世界的抽象。旨在表示更复杂的系统或现象的简化框架。通过去除不必要的细节，模型使我们能够专注于系统的特定方面或动态，从而更容易以受控方式理解、分析和预测行为。模型是通过人类决定要包含和排除哪些数据和参数以及要强调或忽略哪些因果关系来创建的。模型设计者还决定哪些有形的、可测量的数据点将作为更抽象概念的代理。A model is an abstraction of the real world. A simplified framework designed to represent a more complex system or phenomenon. By stripping away unnecessary details, a model allows us to focus on specific aspects or dynamics of a system, making it easier to understand, analyse, and predict behaviour in a controlled manner. Models are created through human decisions about what data and parameters to include and exclude, as well as which cause-and-effect relationships to emphasise or ignore. Model designers also decide what tangible, measurable datapoints will serve as proxies for more abstract concepts.

需要记住的重要一点是，模型不是中立的：它们是人类引导的现实世界的抽象和表示（图 2），由有关数据、框架和重点的决策决定。虽然我们经常认为模型是由数学和算法驱动的，但它们也反映了其创建者的假设和观点。What is critical to remember is that models are not neutral: they are human-guided abstractions and representations of the real world (Figure 2), shaped by decisions about data, framing, and emphasis. While we often think of models as being driven by mathematics and algorithms, they also reflect the assumptions and perspectives of their creators.

99

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场。The Model is Not the Market.

图 2：地图不是领土Figure 2: The Map is Not the Territory.地图制作者（或模型设计师）决定从现实世界中提取哪些数据。模型是由指导这些抽象表示的人设计的。Map makers (or model designers) decide what data to abstract from the real world. Models are designed by people who guide representation of these abstractions.

考虑一张世界地图。每个投影都会根据制图师的决定以某种方式扭曲现实。墨卡托投影扩大了两极附近的陆地面积，而低估了赤道附近的陆地面积。相比之下，加尔-彼得斯投影保留了陆地的比例大小，但扭曲了它们的形状。地图投影凸显了模型设计如何既准确又扭曲（图 3）。Consider a world map. Every projection distorts reality in some way based on the decisions made by the cartographer. A Mercator projection enlarges land masses near the poles and underrepresents those near the equator. In contrast, the Gall-Peters projection preserves the proportional size of landmasses but distorts their shapes. Map projections highlight how model designs can be both accurate and distorting (Figure 3).

同样，在房地产领域，任何估值或预测模型都包含对突出哪些因素和淡化哪些因素的选择。例如，理查兹等人。 [328]表明，向美国公民提供不同的地图投影会导致人们对美国购买格陵兰岛的提议和俄罗斯重要性的看法发生改变。信息的构造和表示方式本质上影响着感知。 [272、316、328]。Similarly, in real estate, any valuation or forecasting model embodies choices about which factors to highlight and which to downplay. For instance, Richards et al. [328], showed that presenting US citizens with different map projections resulted in altered opinions around the US’s proposal to purchase Greenland and the importance of Russia. The way information is structured and represented inherently influences perception. [272, 316, 328].

图 3：对世界的不同表述。两种地图投影都是“准确的”，因为它们遵循在平面上表示球体表面的公认准则。墨卡托投影保留角度，但将区域向两极拉伸。Figure 3: Different representations of the world. Both map projections are “accurate” in that they follow accepted guidelines for representing the surface of a sphere on a flat plane. The Mercator projection preserves angles but stretches areas toward the poles.

100

这些决定背后的政治和社会背景常常被忽视。 2025 年 1 月 20 日，白宫发布 EO 14172，指示联邦机构使用“美洲湾”并更新地名信息系统 (GNIS)。谷歌于 2025 年 2 月 10 日开始通过基于位置的标签反映这一点：美国用户看到“美洲湾”，墨西哥看到“墨西哥湾”，而其他人则看到“墨西哥湾（美洲湾）”[326]。这是一个惊人的提醒：地图（和模型）是由权力和社会压力塑造的。正如命名一个水域可以改变公众的看法一样，将一个社区描述为“优质”与“高风险”可以影响购买模式、贷款决策，甚至城市政策。The political and social context behind these decisions is often overlooked. On Jan 20, 2025, the White House issued EO 14172, directing federal agencies to use “Gulf of America” and to update Geographic Names Information System (GNIS). Google began reflecting this via location-based labels on Feb 10, 2025: US users see “Gulf of America,” Mexico sees “Gulf of Mexico,” and for everyone else "Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America)" [326]. This is a striking reminder that maps (and models) are shaped by power and social pressures. Just as naming a body of water can alter public perception, describing a neighbourhood as “Prime” versus “High Risk” can influence buying patterns, lending decisions, and even urban policy.

从 GPS 导航到信用评分，模型在日常生活中无处不在。在房地产领域，模型支撑着自动估值工具、租金定价算法和贷方风险评估。认识到这些系统是建立在特定数据、假设和优先级之上的，专业人士能够批判性地对待算法输出，而不是认为它是绝对正确的。无论是选择房屋定价模型的功能，还是决定在租户筛选工具中包含哪些风险变量，深思熟虑的模型设计都能带来更公平、更可靠的结果。Models are everywhere in daily life, from GPS directions to credit scores. In real estate, models underpin automated valuation tools, rent-pricing algorithms, and lender risk assessments. Recognising that these systems are built upon specific data, assumptions, and priorities enables professionals to treat algorithmic outputs critically, rather than as infallible. Whether selecting features for a home-pricing model or deciding which risk variables to include in a tenant-screening tool, thoughtful model design fosters fairer, more reliable outcomes.

一个简单的课堂活动，例如调整自动评估模型中的单个因素并观察它如何改变估计价格，可以有力地说明设计选择的影响。通过直接接触这些“杠杆”，学生可以观察建模决策如何影响整个房地产市场，强调负责任和反思性人工智能实践的必要性。A simple classroom activity, like adjusting a single factor in an automated valuation model and observing how it shifts the estimated price, can powerfully illustrate the implications of design choices. By directly engaging with these “levers,” students can observe how modelling decisions ripple across real estate markets, underscoring the need for responsible and reflective AI practices.

3.3.2 当我们将人类从人工智能中心移除时。3.3.2 When we remove humans from the centre of AI.

盲目信任数学模型可能会导致这些模型所服务的人类去中心化。许多例子表明，当数学和人工智能模型应用于复杂的社会系统时，如何通过从其设计中排除某些群体或观点而无意中造成伤害[291]。Placing blind trust in mathematical models risks decentring the very humans such models aim to serve. Many examples show how mathematical and AI models, when applied to complex social systems, can unintentionally cause harm by excluding certain groups or perspectives from their design [291].

虽然这些模型可以提供强大的理解和预测工具，但它们的简化可能会导致重大疏忽，尤其是在应用于人类环境时。下面探讨的一个众所周知的例子说明了这些系统在脱离其社会背景时如何编码和放大结构性偏见。它已成为负责任人工智能讨论的规范参考点，并为教育工作者在转向房地产特定案例之前提供了一个有用的切入点。While these models can offer powerful tools for understanding and prediction, their simplifications can lead to significant oversights especially when applied to human contexts. A well-known example, explored below, illustrates how such systems can encode and amplify structural bias when removed from their social context. It has become a canonical reference point in discussions of responsible AI and offers a useful entry point for educators before turning to real estate-specific cases.

案例研究：风险累犯模型中的偏差。Case Study: Bias in a risk recidivism model.

在美国，法院使用一种名为替代制裁惩教罪犯管理分析 (COMPAS) 的商业风险评估工具来预测囚犯再次犯罪的可能性。 ProPublica 2016 年的一项调查显示，In the United States, a commercial risk assessment tool called the Correctional Offender Management Profiling for Alternative Sanctions (COMPAS) was used by courts to predict the likelihood that a prisoner would reoffend. A 2016 ProPublica investigation revealed that the

101

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场。The Model is Not the Market.

该模型系统地对黑人被告产生偏见，将他们视为未来犯罪的高风险者，其频率是具有相似特征的白人被告的两倍 [13, 14]。model was systematically biased against Black defendants, rating them as high-risk for future crimes twice as often as white defendants with similar profiles [13, 14].

该模型使用了各种输入，包括邮政编码、家庭背景、教育经历以及对诸如“饥饿的人有权偷窃”或“你在学校打架的频率如何？”等陈述的回应。这些数据点充当了“重新犯罪的可能性”这一抽象概念的代理。然后，该模型计算出风险评分，并将其提供给做出假释决定的法官。这种设计的一个主要缺陷是使用了编码历史不平等和系统性歧视的代理。The model used a variety of inputs including postcode, family background, educational history, and responses to statements such as: “A hungry person has the right to steal,” or “How often did you get in fights at school?” These datapoints acted as proxies for the abstract concept of "likelihood of reoffending." The model then calculated a risk score, which was provided to judges making parole decisions. A primary flaw in this design was the use of proxies that encoded historical inequalities and systemic discrimination.

显然，该模型反映了根深蒂固的偏见，将来自某些邮政编码或家庭情况的人视为具有相同的风险状况。这导致了不同的影响，并引发了对刑事司法公平、透明度和问责制的严重担忧。Clearly, the model reflected embedded prejudices, treating people from certain postcodes or family circumstances as though they shared the same risk profile. This resulted in disparate impacts and raised serious concerns about fairness, transparency, and accountability in criminal justice.

通过将该案例中的关键概念提取为结构化格式（表 15），学生可以更好地理解偏差是如何产生的以及应如何审核模型假设。房地产教育工作者可以使用这个例子作为垫脚石，鼓励学生识别和批评住房、估值或贷款模型中的类似问题。By extracting the key concepts from this case into a structured format (Table 15), students can better understand how bias arises and how model assumptions should be audited. Real estate educators can use this example as a stepping stone, encouraging students to identify and critique similar issues in housing, valuation, or lending models.

3.3.3 生成式人工智能模型如何工作3.3.3 How Generative AI models work

本节为希望帮助学生了解人工智能模型如何运作的教育工作者提供技术背景，特别是在房地产背景下[5]。我们经常让计算机通过人类设计的模型来处理数据。就人工智能和机器学习 (ML) 而言，我们有时要求机器搜索新的模式、关系或预测信号。人工智能模型的核心是使用统计技术来识别数值数据中的模式并从中学习。This section offers technical background for educators who want to help students understand how AI models function, particularly in real estate contexts[5] . We frequently task computers to process data through human-designed models. In the case of AI and machine learning (ML), we sometimes ask machines to search for new patterns, relationships, or predictive signals. At their core, AI models use statistical techniques to recognise and learn from patterns in numerical data.

该过程通常首先抽象现实世界的某些部分，将其转换为数字数据，然后应用算法对其进行分析。当模型接受过去数据的训练时，它们会“学习”输入和结果之间的关系。然后，对我们现实世界的数字描述（经过训练的人工智能模型）可以使用它学到的知识在新数据中寻找相似的模式，并提供对我们世界的描述或预测。The process typically begins by abstracting some part of the real world, converting it into numerical data, and then applying algorithms to analyse it. When models are trained on past data, they "learn" relationships between inputs and outcomes. The resulting numerical depiction of our real world (a trained AI model) can then use what it learned to look for similar patterns in new data and provide descriptions or predictions of our world.

“人工智能”一词是一个非常宽泛、定义不明确且不断变化的术语。在本文中，我们将人工智能视为神经网络。神经网络是一种受人脑启发的模型。它由处理数据的互连节点（或“神经元”）层组成。每个节点接收输入，应用加权和和非线性函数（通常称为激活函数），并将结果传递到下一层。通过训练（即根据输出反馈与预期结果相比调整权重），网络通过本质上近似复杂的数学函数来学习识别模式、做出预测或对数据进行分类。The term “AI” is a very broad, poorly defined, and shifting term. In this text, we will consider AI to mean a neural network. A neural network is a type of model inspired by the human brain. It consists of layers of interconnected nodes (or “neurons”) that process data. Each node receives inputs, applies a weighted sum and a non-linear function (often called an activation function), and passes the result to the next layer. Through training (i.e. adjusting the weights based on feedback from the output compared to the expected result) the network learns to recognize patterns, make predictions, or classify data by essentially approximating complex mathematical functions.

在较高的层面上，这个过程可以理解为一系列设计选择，将现实世界的各个方面转化为可计算的形式。关于测量什么、如何表示以及如何权衡变量之间关系的决策都不是中立的。他们决定模型可以“看到”什么以及它如何行动。下图（图 4）提供了此过程的简化表示，突出显示了数据选择、抽象和模型架构如何结合起来形成输出。没有必要遵循图中的每个技术细节。相反，它可以从左到右解读为从输入数据经过层层转换到最终输出的概念流程。关键点是，每个阶段都涉及人类对表示和权重的选择，而这些选择构成了模型最终产生的结果。At a high level, this process can be understood as a sequence of design choices that translate aspects of the real world into computable form. Decisions about what to measure, how to represent it, and how to weight relationships between variables are not neutral. They determine what the model can “see” and how it can act. The diagram below (Figure 4) provides a simplified representation of this process, highlighting how data selection, abstraction, and model architecture combine to shape outputs. It is not necessary to follow every technical detail in the diagram. Instead, it can be read from left to right as a conceptual flow from input data through layers of transformation to final outputs. The key point is that each stage involves human choices about representation and weighting, and these choices structure what the model ultimately produces.

5 本节介绍了 Gen AI 工作原理的基础知识，包含在第 3 章中，因为它是为学术教科书出版而编写的。5 This section on the basics of how Gen AI works is included in Chapter 3 as it was written for publication in an academic text-book.

103

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场。The Model is Not the Market.

图 4：AI 神经网络的模型设计。该图显示了模型设计决策（例如选择属性特征的代理和调整跨层权重）如何直接形成预测。Figure 4: Model Design of an AI Neural Network. This diagram shows how model design decisions, such as selecting proxies for property characteristics and adjusting weights across layers, directly shape predictions.

正如输入网络的数据可能会对结果产生偏差一样，模型设计中的结构选择（例如层数或激活函数）也会对最终输出产生深远的影响。更简单地说，数据和网络的构建方式都决定了神经网络的执行效率和公平程度。Just as the data fed into the network can bias the results, structural choices in model design (such as the number of layers or activation functions) also have a profound impact on the final outputs. More simply, both the data and the way a network is architected shape how effectively and fairly a neural network will perform.

过去几年，人们大肆炒作人工智能模型正在超越社会的各个方面，并将其归咎于其“黑匣子”性质，即内部决策过程不透明且人类难以解释。然而，重要的是要记住，人工智能模型是人类设计的，由人类选择的数据提供，并以某些人类决定的方式应用。模型从根本上来说是人造的，因此人工智能模型的输出和使用的责任完全取决于我们。在图 4 中，我们可以看到人工智能模型的“黑匣子”实际上只是模型内部发生了如此多的计算，以至于人类大脑无法对正在发生的事情做出可用的心理描述。There has been a lot of hype in the last few years about AI models overtaking aspects of society and blame placed on their “black-box” nature, where the internal decisionmaking process is opaque and difficult for humans to interpret. However, it is essential to remember that AI models are human designed, fed by data selected by humans, and applied in ways that some humans decide. Models are fundamentally human made and as such accountability for the outputs and uses of AI models rests squarely with us. In Figure 4, we can see that the “black box” of an AI model is really just that there are so many calculations happening inside the model that it is impossible for the human mind to make a useable mental picture of what is happening.

图 4 还说明了如何将各个数据点（例如房产规模、位置、建筑年龄）转换为价格预测等抽象结果的输入。神经网络中的术语“偏差”是指添加到节点输出的小调整。例如，浴室秤的读数总是高出几磅，这就是“偏差”。这有助于网络将其输出远离零，从而实现更灵活、更准确的模式检测。Figure 4 also illustrates how individual data points (e.g., property size, location, building age) are converted into inputs for abstract outcomes like price predictions. The term "bias" in neural networks refers to a small adjustment added to the output of a node. For example, a bathroom scale that always reads a few pounds too high has a "bias." This helps a network shift its output away from zero, allowing for more flexible and accurate pattern detection.

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场The Model is Not the Market

104

尽管这些计算在数学上是可追溯的，但庞大的运算量可能会导致模型的内部逻辑难以解释。这引发了人们对“黑匣子”人工智能的担忧。然而，重要的是要记住，即使是不透明的模型仍然是由人类构建和操纵的。针对这种不透明性的一种应对措施是开发人工智能系统，在做出最终决定的过程中返回“推理”或中间输出。这些当地的解释仍处于早期阶段，但可能会提高透明度。Although these calculations are mathematically traceable, the sheer volume of operations can render the model's internal logic effectively uninterpretable. This has led to concerns about “black box” AI. However, it is important to remember that even opaque models are still built and steered by humans. One response to this opacity is the development of AI systems that return "reasoning" or intermediate outputs along the way to a final decision. These local explanations are still early-stage but may offer improved transparency.

人工智能模型在房地产领域已经广泛应用。例如，人工智能模型可以使用供应、需求、利率和经济状况代理指标等输入来分析房地产市场趋势。例如，该模型可能会发现，当利率下降时，需求就会增加，如果供应保持不变，就会导致房价上涨。这种类型的预测模型可以为投资者、决策者和规划者提供信息，提供超越传统估值方法的速度和自动化。AI models have become widespread in real estate. For example, an AI model might analyse housing market trends using inputs such as supply, demand, interest rates, and proxy indicators for economic conditions. The model might find, for instance, that when interest rates drop, demand increases, leading to higher home prices if supply remains constant. This type of predictive modelling can inform investors, policymakers, and planners, offering speed and automation beyond traditional valuation methods.

这里的关键要点是，即使是技术含量很高的人工智能系统也是由人类决策决定的。它们的公平性、准确性和社会影响取决于它们的设计、培训和部署的周密程度。The key takeaway here is that even highly technical AI systems are shaped by human decisions. Their fairness, accuracy, and social impact depend on how thoughtfully they are designed, trained, and deployed.

3.4 社会技术映射和偏差3.4 Sociotechnical Mapping and Bias

3.4.1 房地产社会技术系统3.4.1 Sociotechnical Systems in Real Estate

人工智能房地产不仅仅涉及数据和算法，还涉及这些工具如何与人员、机构、市场规范和法规互动。正如地图简化了复杂的地形一样，房地产模型抽象了房地产市场，不可避免地遗漏了细微差别。消除这些系统中的所有偏见是不可能的，尤其是当模型建立在由不平衡的发展、政策和访问形成的历史数据之上时。社会技术映射帮助我们了解房地产中的人工智能工具（例如估值引擎或租户筛选系统）如何受到更广泛的生态系统（包括代理商、买家、贷方和政府机构）的影响。AI-Real Estate is not just about data and algorithms, it’s about how those tools interact with people, institutions, market norms, and regulations. Just as a map simplifies complex terrain, real estate models abstract the property market, inevitably leaving out nuance. Removing all bias from these systems is impossible, especially when models are built on historical data shaped by uneven development, policy, and access. Sociotechnical mapping helps us unpack how AI tools in real estate, like valuation engines or tenant screening systems, are influenced by and influence the broader ecosystem, including agents, buyers, lenders, and government bodies.

当我们谈到人工智能在房地产或房地产科技中的应用时，我们实际上是在创建模型来描述房地产世界，这些模型使用人工智能驱动的技术应用统计方法，根据我们提供给机器的模型和数据进行预测或决策。我们对在这些流程中包含哪些数据的决定直接影响人工智能模型产生的结果，从而影响该模型的输出（图 5）。例如，在人工智能生成的房地产评估报告中，有人决定哪些数据是相关的，哪些数据将被包含或排除。然后，利用人工智能来收集更深入的见解。When we speak of AI applications to real estate or Proptech, we are in reality creating models to describe the world of real estate that use AI-powered technologies to apply statistical methods to make predictions or decisions based on the model and data we provide to the machine. Our decisions of what data to include in these processes directly impacts the results that AI models produce and thus the outputs of that model (Figure 5). For example, in the case of an AI generated property valuation report, someone decides which data is relevant and which will be included or excluded. Then, an AI is employed to glean deeper insights.

105

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场。The Model is Not the Market.

图 5：人类和人工智能的决策介于现实世界和分析输出之间。每当我们从现实世界中提取数据并对其进行操作以获得更深入的见解或预测时，我们都会情不自禁地将观点和偏见纳入最终报告的创建中。Figure 5: Human and AI Decisions Sit Between the Real World and Analysis Outputs. Any time we abstract data from the real world and manipulate it to gain deeper insights or predictions, we cannot help but include perspectives and biases in the creation of the resulting report.

正如 Alfred Korzybski [210] 所说的那样，“地图不是领土”。每个输出都是现实的简化版本，由众多设计选择构建而成。过度拟合参数过多的模型可能会使其变得笨重；相反，规格不足可能会掩盖关键见解。保持这种平衡对于负责任的模型使用至关重要。As Alfred Korzybski [210] famously put it, “The map is not the territory”. every output is a simplified version of reality, built from numerous design choices. Overfitting a model with too many parameters can make it unwieldy; conversely, under-specification can obscure key insights. Navigating this balance is central to responsible model use.

3.4.2 偏见不可避免3.4.2 Bias is inevitable

要真正掌握人工智能技术应用于房地产行业的道德风险，重要的是要理解为什么不可能消除所有偏见。您经常在商业文献中听到，某些组织或人工智能模型的建立是为了“消除”所有偏见：这是一种无意义的说法，表明人们对人工智能技术和模型构建缺乏根本性的理解。有些学生只在表面上了解人工智能的风险，例如输入的数据质量差会导致输出的数据质量差。虽然 GIGO 是故事的重要组成部分，但它并不是故事的全部。To truly grasp the ethical risks of applying AI technologies to the real estate industry, it is important to understand why it is impossible to remove all bias. Often you hear in business literature that some organisation or AI model has been built to “remove” all bias: this is a nonsensical statement that indicates a fundamental lack of understanding of both AI technologies and model building. Some students are only taught about the risks of AI at a superficial level such as poor data going in leads to poor data coming out. Whilst GIGO is an important part of the story, it is not the entire picture.

试图消除模型中的偏见就像试图消除照片中的视角一样：角度总是决定所看到的和遗漏的。Trying to eliminate bias from a model is like attempting to remove the perspective from a photograph: the angle always shapes what’s seen and what’s left out.

声称你可以完全消除人工智能模型中的偏见，就像说你可以设计一座完全不受任何建筑风格或地区影响的房子一样。每栋房屋都不可避免地会反映出受建造者品味、当地传统和实际考虑影响的设计选择。另一个例子可以在人力资源领域找到：即使招聘人员使用结构化面试和评分系统，每个招聘决策都会受到偏见的影响。他们优先考虑的标准，例如经验高于潜力、文化契合度高于多样性、技术技能高于软技能，反映了决定聘用人员的隐含价值观。Claiming that you can completely remove bias from an AI model is like saying you can design a house that’s completely free of any architectural style or regional influence. Every house will inevitably reflect design choices influenced by the builder's taste, local traditions, and practical considerations. Another example can be found in human resources: every hiring decision is influenced by bias, even when recruiters use structured interviews and scoring systems. The criteria they prioritise, such as experience over potential, cultural fit over diversity, or technical skills over soft skills, reflect implicit values that shape who will be hired.

偏见这个词经常被用作有毒偏见的缩写。人工智能模型中的某些偏见，特别是那些强化歧视或伤害的偏见，引发了道德问题。毒性偏向The word bias is often used as short-hand for toxic-bias. Certain biases in AI models, particularly those that reinforce discrimination or harm, raise ethical concerns. Toxic-bias

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场The Model is Not the Market

106

人工智能的应用是一个现实且重要的问题，许多学者和研究人员已经研究了好几年。然而，模型中的偏见并不一定意味着消极或有害的观点；它指的是从数据、算法以及构建或部署模型的人选择的目标中出现的不可避免的有利位置或权重。早期的生成式人工智能模型（GenAI）经常表现出明显的毒性偏差 [2, 127, 192]；而且，虽然大多数科技公司都付出了显着的努力来减轻这些偏见，但它们往往是通过“创可贴”类型的修复来解决的，例如系统提示和内容警告，而不是消除底层模型中的有毒倾向。in AI is a real and significant problem that many scholars and researchers have studied for several years. However, bias in a model doesn’t necessarily imply negative or harmful perspectives; it refers to the inescapable vantage point or weighting that emerges from the data, the algorithms, and the goals chosen by those building or deploying the model. Early Generative AI models (GenAI) often exhibited obvious toxic bias [2, 127, 192]; and, whilst most tech companies have put in notable effort to mitigate these biases, they have often been addressed with “band-aid” type fixes such as system prompts and content warnings rather than removing the toxic proclivities from the underlying model.

人工智能中的偏见不仅仅是一个技术问题，而且是一个背景问题。 RAI 的目标不是消除偏见，而是注重在背景下理解和减轻偏见。把它想象成Bias in AI is not merely a technical problem but a contextual one. Rather than aiming to eliminate bias, RAI focuses on understanding and mitigating it within context. Think of it as理解understanding系统而不是试图the system rather than trying to修复fix系统。人工智能伦理学家专注于识别和承认偏见，评估其在使用模型的特定背景下的潜在有害影响，然后确定是否以及如何减轻这种偏见。这种方法确保该模型保持有效和公平，使其结果与其所服务的社区的需求和价值观保持一致。the system. AI ethicists focus on recognising and acknowledging bias, assessing its potential harmful impacts within the specific context where a model will be used, and then determining whether, and how, that bias should be mitigated. This approach ensures that the model remains both effective and equitable, aligning its outcomes with the needs and values of the communities it serves.

3.4.3 案例研究：Zillow 和算法中的偏差3.4.3 Case Study: Zillow and Bias in Their Algorithm

Zillow 是一家总部位于美国的房地产市场，于 2006 年推出了一款面向公众、由算法驱动的房屋估价工具。该模型依赖于历史数据和人工输入。然而，有缺陷的假设和内在偏差导致了对财产价值的系统性高估。这些不准确之处导致了经济损失并损害了人们对 Zillow 服务的信任[376]。这个案例凸显了人工智能的偏见与开发过程中做出的数据和设计选择深深地交织在一起，强调了透明度和道德监督在人工智能驱动的决策中的重要性。自那时以来，Zillow 取得了重大改进Zillow, a US-based real estate marketplace, launched a public-facing, algorithm-powered home valuation tool in 2006. This model relied on historical data and human-curated inputs. However, flawed assumptions and embedded biases led to systematic overestimations of property values. The inaccuracies resulted in financial losses and damaged trust in Zillow’s services [376]. This case highlights that bias in AI is deeply intertwined with the data and design choices made during development, underscoring the importance of transparency and ethical oversight in AI-driven decision-making. Zillow have made significant improvements since that time

偏差通过数据选择、特征权重和模型架构的选择进入 Zillow 模型。尽管 Zillow 做出了改进，[194]，但它仍然是一个Bias entered the Zillow model through choices about data selection, feature weighting, and model architecture. Although Zillow has made improvements, [194], it is still a型号model现实世界，因此受到挑战和不可避免的偏见。of the real world and as such subject to challenges and inevitable biases.

这个案例说明，即使意图是好的，根深蒂固的偏见也会影响结果。更重要的是，它表明模型并不是现实的中立反映；他们是其中的一部分。用于训练模型的数据与市场行为相互作用，创建影响用户信任和估值结果的反馈循环。This case illustrates how deeply embedded biases can shape outcomes, even when intentions are good. More importantly, it shows that models are not neutral reflections of reality; they are part of it. The data used to train a model interact with market behaviour, creating feedback loops that influence both user trust and valuation outcomes.

Zillow 案例也直接链接回本章的理论框架。如果地图不是领土，那么自动估值模型不仅仅是解读房地产市场，而是帮助组织如何看待和运作该市场。社会技术映射使这一点变得显而易见：训练数据、代理选择、组织激励、用户行为和市场预期都相互作用。从这个意义上说，Zillow 并不是The Zillow case also links directly back to the theoretical frame of this chapter. If the map is not the territory, then an automated valuation model is not simply reading the housing market but helping to organise how that market is seen and acted on. Sociotechnical mapping makes this visible: training data, proxy choices, organisational incentives, user behaviour, and market expectations all interact. In that sense, Zillow is not

107

只是一个不准确预测的例子。这是模型、机构和市场之间递归反馈的情况，其中输出可以塑造后来的行为，从而改变模型要描述的条件。just an example of inaccurate prediction. It is a case of recursive feedback between model, institution, and market, where outputs can shape later behaviour and thereby alter the conditions the model is meant to describe.

3.4.4 使用社会技术图可视化关系3.4.4 Visualising relationships using sociotechnical maps

社会技术系统 (STS) 是一个涉及人类（人和社会）和技术（机器和软件）的模型，旨在绘制这两个关键方面以及其他影响因素之间的关系[117, 395]。 STS 可能包括人类与技术之间的关系以及系统在其中运行的复杂基础设施。图 6 是根据 Emery 和 Trist [117] 关于社会技术系统的原始工作建模的：在其中我们可以看到人、行业结构、计算机系统和我们创建的报告（即财产估值）之间的关系如何以复杂的方式相互作用。A sociotechnical system (STS) is a model that involves humans (people and societies) and technology (machines and software) and seeks to map the relationships between these two key aspects as well as other influencing factors[117, 395]. An STS may include relationships between humans and technology and complex infrastructures that the system operates within. Figure 6 is modelled off Emery and Trist’s [117] original work on sociotechnical systems: in it we can see how the relationships between people, industry structures, computer systems, and the reports we create (i.e. property valuations) can interact in a complex manner.

RAI 中的社会技术映射阐明了人工智能模型、组织、社会结构、个人和行业规范如何相互关联和影响。人工智能模型不是孤立存在的，而是在由人类决策、文化规范和监管框架塑造的特定社会和制度背景下运行。Sociotechnical mapping in RAI illuminates how AI models, organisations, social structures, individuals, and industry norms interconnect and influence one another. Rather than existing in isolation, AI models operate within specific social and institutional contexts shaped by human decisions, cultural norms, and regulatory frameworks.

图 7：人工智能房地产中的社会技术系统思维。这里的要点是不仅要查看图中的对象，还要查看对象之间的关系（例如红色箭头）。虚线代表多孔边界。Figure 7: Sociotechnical Systems Thinking in AI-Real Estate. The takeaway here is to look at not just the objects in the diagram but the relationships (e.g., red arrows) between the objects. The dotted line represents a porous boundary.

了解社会和技术子系统以及它们所处的更广泛的背景系统之间的相互依赖性有助于从业者查明潜在的偏见、权力失衡和道德风险。人工智能房地产系统的社会技术绘图练习可以实现更负责任的设计和部署。Understanding these interdependencies between social and technical subsystems and the broader contextual systems they sit within helps practitioners pinpoint potential biases, power imbalances, and ethical risks. A sociotechnical mapping exercise of AI-Real Estate systems enables more responsible design and deployment.

鼓励学生考虑这些关系（例如上图中的红色箭头）如何运作和影响整个系统也很重要。例如，人员和任务之间的箭头可能是一个依赖于良好用户体验（UX）设计的界面平台。在 AVM 的结构节点和任务之间，我们可能会考虑一种动力动态，即箭头更频繁地朝一个方向或另一个方向移动。It is important to encourage students to also consider how the relationships, for instance the red-arrows in the figure above, might operate and impact the whole system. 人工智能驱动的房地产系统并不是孤立运行的；它们嵌入到涉及人员、机构和行业实践的复杂社会技术系统中。无论是人类还是人工智能系统做出的每一个决策，都受到先验知识、背景影响和制度约束的影响。AI-driven real estate systems do not function in isolation; they are embedded within complex sociotechnical systems that involve people, institutions, and industry practices. Each decision made, whether by a human or an AI system, is shaped by prior knowledge, contextual influences, and institutional constraints.

学生可能会考虑周围复杂环境的哪些方面可能比其他方面对系统产生更大的影响。即使在这个简化的图表中，也有相当多的内容需要解开，这可能会引发有趣的课堂讨论。教育工作者还可以组织任务小组尝试将现实世界的案例应用于此类地图。例如，如果我们采用表 16 中的 Zestimate 案例研究概念，我们可以开始将这些想法应用到 STS 地图中，如图 8 所示。Students might consider which aspects of the surrounding complex environment might have more impact than others on the system. 3.4.5 Feedback loops in AI Systems

STS 的一个关键特征是非线性，超越了简单化的因果关系。这些有时被称为控制论过程，包括反馈循环，有助于识别关系或行为何时相互影响。这些概念通常用于更好地理解人工智能如何在道德上和负责任地符合我们的期望[354]。例如，人工智能模型的数据输入本身就是人类决策的产物。关于衡量什么、如何衡量以及排除什么的决定。然后，人工智能模型处理这些输入，生成见解，并呈现影响人类决策的输出，进而影响下一个数据收集和建模周期。A key feature of STS’s is their non-linearity, moving beyond simplistic cause and effect. These are sometimes called cybernetic process and include feedback loops which help identify when relationships or actions impact on one another. These concepts are often applied to better understand how AI might ethically and responsibly align with our expectations [354]. For example, data inputs into an AI model are themselves products of human decisions. Decisions about what to measure, how to measure it, and what to exclude. AI models then process these inputs, generate insights, and present outputs that influence human decisions, which in turn affect the next cycle of data collection and modelling.

3.4.6 课堂活动：绘制采购建议3.4.6 Class Activity: Mapping Purchasing Recommendations

让学生想象一个房地产平台，该平台使用人工智能根据之前的搜索历史、房产价值和当地设施向潜在买家推荐社区。随着时间的推移，系统可能会开始根据点击率或更快的销售速度来偏向某些社区。这会提高这些区域的可见度，从而推高需求和价格，从而强化算法的偏好。与此同时，其他社区的曝光度较低且停滞不前。Ask students to imagine a real estate platform that uses AI to recommend neighbourhoods to prospective buyers based on previous search history, property values, and local amenities. Over time, the system may begin to favour certain neighbourhoods based on click-through rates or quicker sales. This leads to more visibility for those areas, driving up demand and prices, which in turn reinforces the algorithm’s preference. Meanwhile, other neighbourhoods receive less exposure and stagnate.

3.5 Market Design

3.5.1 模型与现实共建3.5.1 Co-construction of models and reality

模型不仅描述现实，而且还描述现实。他们也可以帮助组织它。在这里，共建意味着递归的社会技术共同塑造：人类假设、制度规则和模型输出相互作用，以便表征反馈到它们本来要描述的市场和行为中。本章中使用的术语就是实际意义上的。它并不意味着模型具有独立的机构，也不意味着论文其他地方对构造的使用都是相同的。经济理论为研究这一现象提供了一个有用的视角，特别是考虑到它长期以来对模型如何影响市场的兴趣。Models do not merely describe reality; they can also help organise it. Here, co-construction means recursive sociotechnical co-shaping: human assumptions, institutional rules, and model outputs interact so that representations feed back into the very markets and behaviours they are meant to describe. The term is used in this chapter in that practical sense. It does not imply that models possess independent agency, nor that every use of construction elsewhere in the thesis is identical. Economic theory offers a useful lens for examining this phenomenon, particularly given its long-standing interest in how models influence markets.

经济学家通常被认为是金融市场的被动观察者。 Yet, increasingly, scholars argue that economic theories and models are performative: they reshape the systems they aim to represent [242].例如，当著名经济学家发布预测或央行根据模型调整利率时，这些行为可以实时改变市场行为。Economists are often thought of as passive observers of financial markets. Yet, increasingly, scholars argue that economic theories and models are performative: they reshape the systems they aim to represent [242]. For example, when a prominent economist publishes a forecast or when central banks adjust interest rates based on a model, these actions can shift market behaviours in real-time.

“经济学通常看起来很抽象……但它也阐明、影响、部署和重组具体经济体的所有混乱的物质性和复杂的社会性。”[Pg.2 242]“Economics often seems abstract. . .yet it also articulates with, influences, is deployed in, and restructures concrete economies in all their messy materiality and their complex sociality.”[Pg.2 242]

The performativity of models is shaped not only by external markets but also by internal academic pressures.正如 MacKenzie [241] 指出的那样，金融理论家努力开发“经济上合理、创新且易于分析处理”的模型。 This dynamic shapes what is considered a “good” model, one that is solvable, publishable, and accepted by peers.The performativity of models is shaped not only by external markets but also by internal academic pressures. As MacKenzie [241] notes, financial theorists strive to develop models that are “economically plausible, innovative, and analytically tractable.” This dynamic shapes what is considered a “good” model, one that is solvable, publishable, and accepted by peers.

方程。然而，一个好的模型也不可能是“显而易见的”，因此存在被理论家同行视为微不足道的风险”[241]equations. However, a good model also could not be “obvious” and thus at risk of being seen by theorists’ peers as trivial” [241]

These institutional and cultural pressures affect the design of economic models, which in turn influence monetary policy. For instance, central banks use models to guide decisions about interest rates.在澳大利亚，2022年5月至2025年2月期间，储备银行加息13次，对住宅和商业房地产市场产生了深刻影响。These institutional and cultural pressures affect the design of economic models, which in turn influence monetary policy. For instance, central banks use models to guide decisions about interest rates. In Australia, the Reserve Bank raised rates 13 times between May 2022 and February 2025, deeply affecting both residential and commercial property markets.

A federal reserve bank may use a combination of models: for example:

But countries around the world differ in this decision: the US aims for 2%, China 3%, India 4%, and SwitzerlandInflation targeting: e.g. in Australia the Reserve Bank has decided on a target of 2%3% [324]. But countries around the world differ in this decision: the US aims for 2%, China 3%, India 4%, and Switzerland下面below 2% [69]. These seemingly small

数值上的差异很重要； they shape expectations, policy responses, and ultimately, how central banks model and manage their economies.numerical differences carry weight; they shape expectations, policy responses, and ultimately, how central banks model and manage their economies.

  • Taylors rule: developed in the US in 1992, this model uses a variety of financial inputs to calculate prescribed interest rates [226]. While widely referenced, its application varies across countries and regimes. For instance, some governments place more weight on inflation, while others emphasise employment or growth. In politically charged contexts, central banks may even be pressured to ignore Taylor-like models entirely.

  • 现金利率目标：用于确定银行之间隔夜利率的模型[325]。虽然许多国家使用现金利率模型来指导短期银行间拆借利率，但其应用方式可能因政治气候、经济意识形态和文化背景而有很大差异。 In some nations, central banks operate with strong independence;在另一些情况下，决策可能反映执政政府的优先事项、强大金融机构的影响力或对通货膨胀、债务和市场干预的更深层次的文化态度。The cash rate target: a model used to determine the overnight interest rates between banks [325]. While the cash rate model is used in many countries to guide short-term interbank lending rates, how it is applied can vary significantly depending on the political climate, economic ideology, and cultural context. In some nations, central banks operate with strong independence; in others, decisions may reflect the priorities of the ruling government, the influence of powerful financial institutions, or deeper cultural attitudes toward inflation, debt, and market intervention.

Whether these policies are justified or not, they demonstrate that economic models directly shape the economies they describe.由于利率和通货膨胀深刻影响房地产市场，这些模型与房地产估值、开发和融资中使用的人工智能系统紧密相连。图 11 使用 STS 地图显示了一些反馈循环类型，其中包含影响房地产行业的经济模型。Whether these policies are justified or not, they demonstrate that economic models directly shape the economies they describe. And because interest rates and inflation deeply affect real estate markets, these models are tightly linked to the AI-powered systems used in property valuation, development, and financing. 3.5.2 政府的市场设计3.5.2 Market Design by Governments

“Market design” refers to deliberate structuring of systems to guide participant behaviour;一些学者称之为“智能市场”[130, 198]。政府经常采取这种形式的结构化干预。例如，2020年3月，美国政府利用美国国债拍卖来平滑价格波动[330]。由于这种市场操纵方法对社会的影响，市场设计被一些学者视为社会工程的一种形式[330]。“Market design” refers to deliberate structuring of systems to guide participant behaviour; what some scholars call “smart markets” [130, 198]. Governments often engage in this form of structured intervention. For example, in March 2020 the US government used US treasury auctions to smooth out price swings [330]. Due to the impact on society of this method of market manipulation, market design has been seen by some scholars as a form of social engineering [330].

新加坡政府土地销售 (GLS) 计划使用精心设计的拍卖将公有土地分配给私人开发商[221]。根据 GLS，政府释放特定的地块（每块地块都有指定的使用限制和开发指南），然后邀请符合资格的开发商在透明的范围内竞标。Singapore’s Government Land Sales (GLS) programme uses carefully designed auctions to allocate publicly owned land to private developers[221]. Under GLS, the government releases specific land parcels (each with designated use restrictions and development guidelines), then invites eligible developers to bid within a transparent

第3章：Chapter 3:模型不是市场The Model is Not the Market

116

拍卖或招标制度[221]。这种设置体现了“智能市场”方法，因为它依赖于结构化规则和机制，就像市场设计学者所倡导的鼓励竞争性但有序的投标一样。此外，它们还可以揭示真实的市场需求，并通过精确控制建设内容和时间，帮助政府实现更广泛的城市规划目标（例如平衡增长和住房供应）。auction or tender system[221]. This setup exemplifies a “smart market” approach because it relies on structured rules and mechanisms much like those advocated by market design scholars to encourage competitive yet orderly bidding. As well, they can reveal true market demand and help the government achieve broader urban-planning goals (e.g., balanced growth and housing availability) through precise control over what is built and when.
